items.longBusinessSummary: Robinhood Markets, Inc. operates financial services platform in the United States. The company's platform allows users to invest in stocks, exchange-traded funds (ETFs), and American depository receipts. It offers fractional trading, recurring investments, access to investing on margin, fully-paid securities lending, cash sweep, instant withdrawals, retirement program, around-the-clock trading, joint investing accounts, event contracts, future contract services, and short selling. The company also provides various learning and education solutions comprise Snacks, an accessible digest of business news stories for a new generation of investors; Learn, which is an online collection of guides, feature tutorials, and financial dictionary; Newsfeeds that offer access to free, premium news from sites from various sites, such as Barron's, Reuters, and Dow Jones. In addition, the company offers In-App Education, a resource that covers investing fundamentals, including why people invest, a stock market overview, and tips on how to define investing goals, as well as allows customers to understand the basics of investing before their first trade; and Crypto Learn and Earn, an educational module available to various crypto customers through Robinhood Learn to teach customers the basics related to cryptocurrency. Further, it provides Robinhood credit cards, cash card and spending accounts, and wallets. Robinhood Markets, Inc. was incorporated in 2013 and is headquartered in Menlo Park, California.

Title: BTC Vs. TAO: Jason Calacanis Says Bitcoin Will Never Hit New Highs, Backs Bittensor Instead
Author: Anushka Basu   Tue, October 27, 2026 at 9:58 AM GMT+1 4 min read
Published: 2026-10-27T08:58:45+00:00
=== BODY ===
Jason Calacanis told his followers on Tuesday to sell Bitcoin and move into artificial intelligence.
The all-in co-host said he is long Bittensor's Tau, a token tied to a decentralized AI network.
He called ETF outflows a warning sign, but spot Bitcoin ETFs drew around $110 million on Monday after seeing two days of outflows.
Angel investor Jason Calacanis, an early investor in Uber (UBER) and Robinhood (HOOD), told his followers to sell Bitcoin (BTC) and invest in artificial intelligence on Tuesday, but said he was long Bittensor (TAO).
Bitcoin's rough stretch was just getting started, the All-In podcast co-host wrote on X. "A brutal year for Bitcoin is just getting started," he wrote.
See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox
Calacanis said Bitcoin could revisit its 2026 low within a year. "We will test the 57k low again in the next 12 months," he wrote. He also said Bitcoin "will never break its all-time high again."
His argument is that money works best where it grows fastest. Calacanis said there are plenty of faster-growing places for investors to put capital today. He said Bitcoin was a "dead network that offers nothing beyond a store of value".
Calacanis said that "The viral nature of bitcoin was it's power... if you didn't own you were MOCKED!" He thinks the promise of changing the world has moved from Bitcoin to AI. He wrote, "Just sell and shift from Bitcoin to Super Intelligence because one provides little to no value, and the other provides unlimited upside for humanity."
Calacanis said one telling sign was the Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs). "Outflows from ETFs are signal and will continue," he wrote.
According to data from SoSoValue, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs saw net outflows amounting to $635.6 million on Oct. 22. That was the largest one-day withdrawal since June 25. The selling didn't last. The funds attracted $110.34 million on Monday, ending two straight sessions of outflows, data from SoSoValue showed.
However, he was not completely rooting against crypto. Calacanis named his AI bet, saying, "I am long $TAO and love Bittensor's focus on scaling AI."
Bittensor is a decentralized network that uses TAO to reward machine learning algorithms that offer AI services. TAO's price edged up over 0.2% at the time of writing. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around TAO dropped to 'extremely bearish' from the 'bearish' zone, with chatter around it at 'normal' levels over the past day. According to platform data, message volume around Bittensor has increased over 60% in a week.
On Stocktwits, Bitcoin was among the top trending tickers at the time of writing. Bitcoin's price was trading around $79,680, down 0.3% in the last 24 hours. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around Bitcoin remained in the 'bearish' zone, accompanied by 'normal' chatter levels over the past day. According to platform data, message volume around Bitcoin has increased over 28% over the past week.
The biggest upgrade to Bitcoin this year was to the software that most people use to run the network. Introduced in April, it modifies how the network organizes the queue of transactions awaiting processing. That should make it more orderly to decide which payments go through next, and replace a stuck payment with a higher-fee version. The update also added an optional way to send payments more privately. July saw a smaller follow-up that fixed bugs.
The clearest first-hand record this year for Bittensor is not about the network itself. According to Grayscale's filing, its Bittensor fund increased its holdings from 36,193 to 38,289.6 TAO in the first quarter, and TAO's price rose from around $220 to around $307 during that period alone. However, investors still can't redeem their shares for the token, pending regulatory approval.
BTC's price is down over 9% so far this year, while TAO's price has gained over 12% year-to-date.

Title: Cowboy Space Reveals Big Iron, Its Data Center Rocket, and Opens Commercial Launch to Government and Third-Party Payloads
Author: Business Wire   Tue, October 27, 2026 at 3:30 AM GMT+1 3 min read
Published: 2026-10-27T02:30:00+00:00
=== BODY ===
Purpose built to put compute in orbit, the vehicle will carry more than 15,000 kg per launch and fly third-party payloads to help ease a national shortage of launch capacity
SAN CARLOS, Calif., October 27, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Cowboy Space Corporation, the orbital infrastructure company founded by Robinhood co-founder Baiju Bhatt, today unveiled the architecture of its launch vehicle, "Big Iron," whose upper stage is designed to stay in orbit as a megawatt-class data center. The company also introduced "Big Iron Express," a commercial launch program for outside customers who need megawatt-class power in orbit, whether for compute or other uses.
"We set out to build data centers in space and found there weren't enough rockets to get them there, so we're building our own," said Baiju Bhatt, founder and CEO of Cowboy Space Corporation. "Our design puts us on a path to cost parity with terrestrial data centers, so that orbital compute costs less than AI compute on the ground. Opening it to the rest of the industry makes every flight safer and more efficient, and gives the country another path to orbit."
Cowboy designed Big Iron around the single purpose of putting data centers in space, which makes it simpler and more efficient to build and fly than a general-purpose vehicle. To further optimize the cost and production speed, many of the rocket's features serve dual-purposes depending on whether it is on ascent or in orbit. For example, Big Iron's skin becomes the data center's radiator; the ammonia propellant becomes the coolant; and the nitrogen pressurizing the rocket's second stage deploys the satellite's solar wings.
The key to Cowboy's design is that rather than deploying a small satellite and being discarded, the upper stage joins Cowboy's constellation, so every launch grows its compute capacity at a cost competitive price. Once deployed at dawn-dusk orbit, the satellite is 132 meters by 73 meters and can carry five compute racks of NVIDIA Vera Rubin GPUs. The same upper stage will be designed to carry other companies' payloads, configured to suit each mission.
The stainless steel vehicle with a reusable booster stands 86 meters tall and is designed to carry more than 15,000 kg to sun-synchronous orbit. It is sized to the limit of road transport, which speeds production and keeps capital costs down. The first stage is powered by nine liquid oxygen and methane "Clydesdale" engines, each of which provides 300,000 lbs of thrust. Cowboy selected methane to support reuse, and chose a gas generator engine cycle, a proven architecture, to shorten the path to first flight.
Cowboy has filed an application with the FCC for a 20,000-satellite constellation called Stampede. The company launched its first satellite, Reason-1, on October 1 to demonstrate laser power beaming from orbit to Earth. Reason-2, slated for 2027, will operate GPUs in orbit for commercial and government workloads, processing data where it's collected and sending results to Earth. Cowboy is targeting its first flight of Big Iron in 2028 and intends to scale its Stampede constellation rapidly thereafter.
Companies interested in "Big Iron Express" launch services can learn more at www.cowboyspace.com.
Cowboy Space Corporation (formerly Aetherflux) is building vertically integrated orbital infrastructure for the AI era, spanning launch vehicles, space-based power, and in-orbit compute. The company is headquartered in San Carlos, California, with operations in Seattle, Washington, and backed by Index Ventures, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Construct Capital, Interlagos, and IVP, among others.
